title: Correction to Hormesis as a Geometric Necessity of Bounded Adaptive Systems
subtitle: Proposed author corrigendum for DOI 10.1177/15593258261469171
author: Daniel John Murray
visual_review: See the hash-bound final visual coverage and author-review receipts.
summary: Proposed correction to the necessity, universal peak-location and finite-change attenuation statements in the published article. It replaces threshold ordering as a sufficient condition with the exact equal-slope initial-derivative condition, states the parameter-dependent peak, corrects finite series attenuation, and retains the adopted bounded-composition framework.
affected_claims: Threshold ordering and high-dose damage do not by themselves imply a beneficial interval.
A universal peak near twice the activation threshold is withdrawn at its stated generality.
Local metabolic-control derivatives cannot be extrapolated to finite enzyme changes without a kinetic model.
The full product shortcut has no universal conservative interpretation or error bound without calibration.
Detectable zone widths require both threshold crossings and a stated cutoff and control.
Finite series-model flux ceilings do not predict the distribution of hormesis peaks.
The common-shape equal-midpoint model does not imply a beneficial interval.
conditions: Equal positive linear-dose logistic slopes for the stated exact primary-model condition and peak
Positive repair and damage amplitudes with greater eventual damage
Specified equal-resistance series model for the corrected finite attenuation
editorial_scope: Journal handling and final corrigendum wording remain subject to editorial review.
